Prompt injection risk: untrusted user brief/details are concatenated into an LLM-directed prompt (including instructions) in PrototypeCreationForm, so crafted input like 'ignore previous instructions' can steer the model despite UI intent. Consider stronger separation (strict data schema + system-side instruction framing) and/or post-LLM policy enforcement for branch/commit/push behaviors. --- General fix: preserve strict separation between **instructions** and **user data** in the generated prompt so user text is treated as payload, not directives. In this file, the best low-impact mitigation is to serialize user inputs into structured JSON and wrap them with explicit non-instruction markers, while keeping trusted instructions in separate sections.

Best single-file fix in hub/app/javascript/features/prototype-creation-form/index.tsx:

  • Replace the current prompt assembly on lines 84–86.
  • Build a userPayload object from brief, details, and selected template metadata.
  • Serialize with JSON.stringify(userPayload) and prepend a clear “data only” header.
  • Keep data.promptInstructions and templateInstructions as separate sections before the payload.
  • This does not change functionality (still passes same semantic content) but materially reduces prompt-injection susceptibility by clarifying boundaries.

No new imports are needed.
